name: Christmas Cactus
description: A long-lived Brazilian rainforest cactus that can be passed down through generations, Christmas Cactus produces cascades of tubular flowers in pink, red, white, orange, or purple at the ends of its segmented, leaf-like stems during winter months. Unlike desert cacti, this epiphyte naturally grows on trees in humid forests and requires more water and less sun. The flat, jointed stems create an attractive trailing or arching form that looks beautiful in hanging baskets or on pedestals. With proper care including a rest period and cool fall temperatures, it reliably blooms during the holidays and can live for 20-30 years or more, becoming a cherished family heirloom that grows more spectacular with age.
toxicity: Non-toxic to cats, dogs and horses.
temperature: 70-80°F (21-27°C) while growing; cool 55-65°F nights in fall set flower buds
careInstructions: Water when top inch of soil is dry - more frequently than desert cacti
Use a well-drained, peat-rich mix - e.g. 1 part potting soil, 2 parts peat moss, 1 part perlite or sharp sand
Provide bright, indirect light - a few hours of morning sun is fine, but full sun bleaches the stems
To trigger blooming, from mid-September give it 13 hours of total darkness each night and 55-65°F nights for 6-8 weeks (nights of 45-55°F set buds even without the darkness)
Water a little less from late August through September, then resume normal watering once flower buds start to swell
Reduce watering again after it finishes flowering
Fertilize monthly spring through summer with diluted balanced fertilizer
Avoid moving plant once buds form - causes bud drop
commonProblems: Bud drop: Plant moved after bud formation, temperature fluctuations, or inconsistent watering
No blooms: Needs fall rest period with longer darkness and cooler temps
Limp, shriveled stems: Underwatering or root rot from overwatering
Red or purple stem edges: Too much direct sun - move to shadier spot
Stem segments falling off: Normal propagation method or severe stress

fertilizing.tip: Fertilize monthly spring through summer with diluted balanced fertilizer

repotting.tip: Repot at least every 4-5 years into fresh mix — old peat-based mix breaks down and suffocates the roots.
repotting.soil: 1 part potting soil, 2 parts peat moss, 1 part perlite or sharp sand

whatsNormal: Buds drop after moving the plant, drafts, temperature swings (especially above 90°F) or uneven watering — leave it in place once buds form.
If it won't bloom, lamps at night in autumn are the usual cause — it needs long, dark nights.
Blooms around Christmas; Thanksgiving cacti, with pointed stem segments, bloom a few weeks earlier.
Can live for decades — some are passed down through families.

propagation.tip: Let cuttings of 1-3 stem segments dry for 2-3 days, then root them in well-drained mix.

flags.note: Toxicity: NC State says Schlumbergera × buckleyi is non-toxic and safe with pets and children; the horse rating comes from ASPCA's S. bridgesii entry.
Winter watering interval (10 days) is our estimate — the sources only say to reduce watering from fall to late winter.
Changed: ideal temperature 60-70°F → 70-80°F while growing; bloom-trigger instructions, soil mix and light guidance now follow all three sources.

Watering timing — resolved by majority: NC State and Wisconsin cut back in late summer/September and again after flowering; MOBOT cuts back from late winter to spring. Set to the NC State/Wisconsin timing.
